Design for REQ-006 is written: `aiws/work/REQ-006/02-design.md` and `aiws/work/REQ-006/api-contract.yaml` (`paths: {}`, no API change). I did not write `03-test-spec.md`; that belongs to the test-designer. Bash was denied in this run, so the YAML parse check and `git status` did not run. I confirmed the nine headings by search, checked the contract against the validator's rule by reading it, and wrote only the two files in scope. ## Key decisions - **D1 – empty-state sentence:** `renderCustomerTable(customers, statusFilter = '')`. The default keeps "Chưa có khách hàng.", so the existing untagged empty-state test passes unmodified; any selected filter gives "Không có khách hàng nào khớp lựa chọn lọc." - **D2 – which filter value:** `refresh()` reads `filterEl.value` once, just before calling the loader, and passes it to the table. The loader is untouched, because adding the value to its result would break five REQ-005 tests (TC-130..TC-134). - **D3/D4 – double click while filtering:** a new pure function `chooseStatusClickKey` returns one shared key (a `Symbol`) while a filter is selected and the customer `id` under "Tất cả". `createDoubleClickGuard.js` and TC-108..TC-113 are unchanged. - **D5/D6 – notice after add:** a new pure function `describeCreateNotice` returns "Đã thêm khách hàng." only when filtering and the created customer's `status` differs from the filter. It is null-safe, since a non-JSON 2xx body would otherwise make a saved customer show "Không lưu được khách hàng." The notice goes in a new `

`, cleared by one `clearMessages()` helper at the six places that clear `#message` today. - **D7–D9 – the four test findings:** - F1: only the `insertByStatuses` helper changes, to use the four standard customers. - F2/F3: assertions are added to TC-120 and TC-122, comparing `JsonNode` values. - F4: `notFound500` is renamed `internalError500`. - Run counts must stay at 173 / 107 / 399. - **D10 – TC codes:** new codes start at TC-135; TC-117, TC-118, TC-120, TC-122 and TC-127 are redefined in the REQ-006 test spec, following the REQ-004 precedent. ## What a reviewer must know - **Five approved decisions change:** - Reversed: REQ-005 D10 option A (no double-click block while filtering) and two consequences of REQ-005 D9 (empty-state sentence, no notice after add). - Narrowed: REQ-004 D1 (per-customer window) now holds only under "Tất cả". - Loosened: REQ-005 D9's rule against capturing `filterEl.value`, for one local variable in `refresh()`. D2 gives the alternative that keeps D9's wording. - **Accepted consequence (Q2):** while filtering, a deliberate click on another customer within 500 ms of a processed click is silently ignored. - **Filter changed between two clicks (Q3):** the two modes keep separate marks, so a click right after switching between "Tất cả" and a filter is not blocked (R3). - **Still not blocked:** triple clicks and impatient re-clicks on a slow network; while filtering these can hit the next customer (R4). - **Never reproduced:** the double-click case in the requirement has no manual record in the repo. Manual steps 1–2 reproduce it before and after the fix. - **Review by diff:** the "tighter" half of AC-5 and AC-6 cannot be shown by running tests, and the orchestrator's "TC code present" check already passes before any change. The five test diffs must be read. - **Task order:** FE-2, FE-3 and FE-4 all edit `main.js` and must run sequentially; one 8-file task is the alternative. - **Deploy:** FE only, with `index.html` and `src/` deployed and rolled back together. A new `main.js` on an old `index.html` throws in every handler. - **Notice timing:** the notice is set before `await refresh()`, not after, so a user action during the reload still clears it. ## Options left for the approver - **TC-119:** left untouched, so the four standard rows appear twice in `CustomerServiceTest.java`. - **F2:** does not assert the concrete phone values of ids 2 and 3. - **Notice condition:** shown only when the new customer is hidden by the filter, not after every successful add. - **Notice colour:** green `#166534` via a new `.notice` rule.
